entries.answer:
1. [lines 121–127, `remaining` / `model_timeout`] — The timeout is calculated before `get_context()` and prompt construction, then can be forced to at least 1.0 second; consequently, when less than one second remains—or when context retrieval consumes most of the remaining time—the model call can run past `wall_clock_timeout_s`.[1]
2. [lines 96 and 224–231, `while step < max_steps and self.running`] — If `self.running` becomes `False` without an `asyncio.CancelledError` being raised, the loop exits and `_execute_task()` returns without marking the dequeued task done, failed, or requeued.[1]
3. [lines 137–141, final-answer path] — Failure of `_record_event(..., "reflection", ...)` is caught and only logged, but the task is then marked done; a completed task can therefore lack its required success/reflection event.[1]
4. [lines 174–180 and 194–204, tool-success path] — `breaker.record_success()` executes before `_record_event()` persists the tool result; if event persistence fails after a successful tool execution, the generic exception handler records a breaker failure and treats the already-successful call as a failed call.[1]
5. [lines 174–180 and 194–204, tool-success path] — If `_record_event()` fails after the tool has executed, `transient_failures` is incremented and the task loop retries, causing the model trajectory to continue as though the tool invocation failed even though its side effect may already have occurred.[1]
6. [line 269, livelock signature] — Converting every tool-argument value to `str(v)` makes distinct values share a signature, such as `1` and `"1"`; distinct actions can therefore be misclassified as repeated actions and trigger a false livelock abort.[1]
7. [lines 83–84, `self.config.agent`] — `config` is typed as `Any` and no `agent` attribute is validated before access; an absent or incompatible `config.agent` raises `AttributeError` before the task-level `try` block begins, leaving the dequeued task without a terminal scheduler update.[1]
8. [line 207, `self.config.checkpoint`] — No `checkpoint` attribute is validated before access; an absent or incompatible `config.checkpoint` raises `AttributeError` inside the transient-error path, repeatedly consumes task steps, and prevents checkpoint creation.[1]
9. [lines 244–254, `_verify_intent_action`] — Final-answer validation checks only the truthiness of `action.final_answer`; any truthy non-string value is accepted and passed to `scheduler.mark_done()` and event payload storage as an answer, despite no string-type validation.[1]
10. [lines 254–258, `_verify_intent_action`] — Tool-call validation requires only that each mapping contain a truthy `"name"` value; it does not require that the name be a string or that `"args"` be a mapping, so malformed calls pass verification and are rejected only later during execution-loop processing.[1]
11. [lines 157–167, malformed tool-call handling] — Malformed tool calls are recorded and skipped without incrementing `transient_failures`, failing the task, or requeuing it; an action containing only malformed calls consumes a full loop iteration with no executable work or terminal state change.[1]
12. [lines 168–173, circuit-open handling] — A circuit-open tool call is appended as a result but does not increment `transient_failures`, delay, fail, or requeue the task; repeated model output of that unavailable call can consume steps until `max_steps` is reached.[1]
13. [lines 205–206, `tool_batch_result`] — A batch event is emitted only when `tool_results` is nonempty; an action whose tool calls are all malformed or rejected before result appending has individual error events but no batch-level result event, producing an incomplete execution record.[1]
14. [lines 232–234, cancellation handler] — `scheduler.mark_failed(task_id, "Cancelled")` is awaited while handling cancellation; if that scheduler call raises, the cancellation path exits with the scheduler update incomplete and the original cancellation is replaced by the scheduler exception.[1]
15. [lines 224–231, max-step terminal path] — After `mark_failed(task_id, "Max steps exceeded")`, the method does not return; any exception from that call is caught by the outer handler, which performs a second `mark_failed()` attempt with a different error message, creating conflicting terminal-state attempts.[1]
16. [lines 85–90, invalid configuration paths] — Failures from `scheduler.mark_failed()` for invalid `max_steps` or invalid `timeout_s` occur before the enclosing task-level `try` block and escape without rollback, cleanup of `task_recent_actions`, or a fallback task-state update.[1]
17. [lines 91–95, pre-`try` task initialization] — Exceptions while initializing task execution before line 95, including `task.id` or configuration-property access failures, bypass `_execute_task()`’s fatal-error handler and do not clean up task state or mark the task failed.[1]
18. [lines 145–154, livelock terminal path] — If `requeue_with_backoff(task_id)` fails after a successful rollback, the exception is caught by the inner transient-error handler and the same task execution continues rather than producing a definite requeue or terminal failure.[1]
19. [lines 101–110, timeout terminal path] — If rollback fails on timeout, the code still marks the task failed and returns, allowing a task to enter a terminal failed state despite an unsuccessful rollback and without recording rollback failure as task state.[1]
20. [lines 226–231, max-step terminal path] — If rollback fails after max steps, the exception is silently discarded with `except Exception: pass`, then the task is marked failed despite the failed rollback and without any failure event or error record.[1]
21. [lines 235–241, fatal-error handler] — If `scheduler.mark_failed()` fails in the fatal-error handler, the exception is silently discarded; the task can remain nonterminal after a fatal execution error.[1]
22. [lines 70–72, main-loop exception handler] — An exception from `record_error("agent_loop_fatal")` is not handled and terminates `run()` instead of allowing the agent loop to log, back off, and continue.[1]
23. [lines 216–223, transient-error handler] — An exception from `record_retry()` is not handled within the handler and escapes to the outer task-level fatal handler, converting a transient operational failure into task failure.[1]
24. [lines 181–191 and 194–204, tool-error handlers] — Exceptions from `record_error("tool_execution")` or `_record_event()` inside either tool-error handler escape that handler and are treated by the broader task-loop exception handler, so an error-observability failure changes the control flow from tool-level recovery to task-level retry.[1]
25. [lines 128–135, invalid model action path] — An invalid action raises or is rejected and only retries; no model-output error event is written for `None`, wrong `ModelAction` type, or failed intent/action verification beyond the latter’s mismatch event, leaving invalid-model failures incompletely recorded.[1]
26. [lines 155–206, `tool_results`] — Tool results are accumulated and persisted as events but are never incorporated directly into the next model prompt; continuation depends entirely on undocumented behavior of `MemoryManager.get_context()` reading the just-appended events, so tool-output feedback is an unresolved/broken dependency.[1]
27. [lines 9–27, external imports] — The module depends on ten project-local modules/packages (`models.model_client`, `memory_manager`, `tool_sandbox`, `scheduler`, `checkpoint`, `observability`, and four `utils.*` modules) whose existence and exported symbols are not provided; module import and all referenced interfaces are unresolved dependencies.[1]
END OF ERROR LIST.
